title: Fulani Braids Tutorial
metaDescription: How to do Fulani braids step by step — the cornrow-and-hanging-braid combo that works beautifully on natural 4A-4C hair and holds for 4-6 weeks.

steps.name: Prep and section
steps.text: Wash and deep condition the hair first, then blow-dry or stretch it so it is easier to cornrow evenly. Part off a center strip from front to back, then divide the rest of the head into large panels with clips.

steps.name: Cornrow the center
steps.text: Cornrow the center strip flat against the scalp, feeding in braiding hair as you go, from the front hairline to the nape.

steps.name: Add the side cornrows
steps.text: Cornrow two to four rows on each side of the center strip, curving them to frame the face. These rows stay flat against the scalp like a traditional cornrow.

steps.name: Drop the hanging braids
steps.text: From the outer sections, braid regular hanging box braids using the pre-stretched hair, working from root to tip in three even strands.

steps.name: Seal and finish
steps.text: Dip the ends in warm water to seal, or use small elastic bands. Apply a light braid spray to reduce frizz and lay the edges with a soft brush.

tips.question: Can I do Fulani braids on short natural hair?
tips.answer: Yes, as long as the hair is at least 2-3 inches long — the added braiding hair carries most of the length, so the cornrow base doesn't need to be long, just long enough to grip.

tips.question: How long do Fulani braids realistically last?
tips.answer: With a satin bonnet at night and light oil on the scalp every few days, 4-6 weeks is realistic before the new growth at the root makes them look messy.

tips.question: Is this doable alone, on my own head?
tips.answer: The center cornrow section is manageable solo with practice, but the side rows and hanging braids are much easier — and faster — with a second pair of hands.

storyIntro: Fulani braids are the style that shows up on every braid inspiration board for a reason — a flat cornrowed center with hanging box braids on the sides, usually finished with a few beads or gold cuffs near the face.

They're a protective style at heart: the cornrowed base means less daily manipulation of the natural hair underneath, which is why they hold up so well for weeks at a time on coily and kinky textures.
storyNote: Stretch the hair before braiding — cornrowing over shrunk, unstretched coils is where most of the tension headaches (and eventual breakage) come from.
